summary: Lolo NF Mineral County crow's-nest station, built 1925, abandoned 1948; the brief's 'gone' status should read abandoned.

facts.design: log cabin with a crow's nest (1925); a 1928 report planned a lookout cabin and a tower
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1948; no source records removal or destruction.

events.note: Watchman Lee L. Mauer struck by lightning at a station the paper calls the Bear Creek lookout; telephone demolished
Daily Missoulian listed a planned lookout cabin and tower at Bear Gulch among new structures
Lookout John Mattovich shot a 90-pound mountain lion on patrol, per a Missoulian report

evidence.supports: built 1925 as a log cabin with a crow's nest; abandoned 1948
1925 log cabin and crow's nest; Mineral County, Lolo National Forest
1928 planned lookout cabin and tower at Bear Gulch
evidence.quote: Among the new structures: Bear Gulch, where there will be a lookout cabin and a tower.

evidence.supports: 1926 watchman struck by lightning at the Bear Creek lookout station near Superior
evidence.quote: Lee L. Mauer, employed at the Bear Creek lookout station between Cedar Creek and Trout Creek near Superior, was struck by lightning about 11:30 in the morning Tuesday, rendering him unconscious for an hour and a half, according to Mauer.

evidence.supports: the lightning demolished the station telephone
evidence.quote: He also discovered that the telephone had been demolished by the lightning

evidence.supports: 1935 lookout at the Bear Gulch station shot a mountain lion on patrol
evidence.quote: John Mattovich, a lookout located at the Bear Gulch station, five miles southeast of Superior, brought down a 90-pound mountain lion Monday night, it was learned here yesterday.

evidence.supports: 1935 lookout met the lion while on patrol and shot it
evidence.quote: Mattovich had just left his station on patrol duty when he encountered the animal and shot him.

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Lookout Association list records the status as Abandoned

corrections.why: Sources record the station as abandoned in 1948, and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list gives its status as Abandoned. No source says it was removed or destroyed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief gives two coordinate pairs. The Forest Fire Lookout Association index gives 47.11773, -114.92780, which matches the record. The second pair came from a source not opened in this run.
The 1925 entries describe a log cabin with a crow's nest. The 1928 report mentions a cabin and a tower. The sources do not say whether these describe the same structure.
The 1926 article calls the station the Bear Creek lookout station; the Montana list files the item under Bear Gulch.

notes_for_editor: The brief's kind 'platform' is consistent with the index type 'Crowsnest', so it was not changed. The 1935 article places the station 'five miles southeast of Superior'; check the brief's coordinates against that direction on a map before publishing. The second coordinate pair was not checked. No present-day site description, photos, or access information were found.
